news.title: Parliament passes new coalition budget after overnight vote
news.text: The lower house passed the coalition budget by 212 votes to 198 after an overnight session. The plan raises defence spending by 4 percent and freezes fuel duty for a year. Opposition parties said they would challenge parts of it in court. The finance minister said the budget keeps the deficit under 3 percent of output, in line with the bloc's rules. Markets reacted calmly, with the benchmark bond yield little changed on the day. The upper house votes next week and is expected to approve it without changes.

news.title: Ceasefire talks resume in Geneva with new mediators
news.text: Delegations returned to Geneva on Monday for a third round of ceasefire talks, with Swiss and Omani mediators now leading the sessions. Officials said the main sticking point is control of the border crossing, which carries about 40 percent of aid deliveries. A pause in fighting held for a fourth day, the longest since the spring. Diplomats cautioned that a deal could still take weeks.

news.title: Gold hits record above $3,700 as dollar slides
news.text: Gold rose 1.2 percent to a record 3,712 dollars an ounce as the dollar index fell to a four-month low. Traders now price two rate cuts by March after weaker jobs data. Silver gained 2 percent and central bank buying continued, with Poland and India the largest buyers this quarter, according to the World Gold Council. Analysts at two banks raised their year-end targets to 3,900 dollars.

news.title: Bitcoin slips 3% as ETF outflows reach a monthly high
news.text: Bitcoin fell 3 percent to about 61,800 dollars after spot ETF funds recorded 480 million dollars of net outflows on Friday, the largest in a month. Smaller tokens fell more. Futures open interest dropped 8 percent, which suggests leveraged traders were forced out. Some analysts see support near 60,000 dollars.

news.title: Central bank holds rates, signals cut in spring
news.text: The central bank kept its policy rate at 4.25 percent for a third meeting and said inflation was easing faster than forecast, at 2.6 percent in October. Governors signalled a cut in spring if wage growth keeps slowing. The currency weakened 0.4 percent after the statement.

news.title: Local election results confirm record turnout
news.text: Final results from Sunday's local elections show 63 percent turnout, the highest in 20 years. The governing party kept 14 of 20 city halls but lost the capital to an independent. Analysts linked the swing to housing costs.
